question.text: Which of the following activities is an NRI explicitly PROHIBITED from undertaking in the Indian securities market?

answer.text: Investing in mutual fund schemes on a repatriable basis
Short selling of securities and trading in the currency derivatives segment
Purchasing equity shares of listed companies through a PINS account
Maintaining separate demat accounts for repatriable and non-repatriable investments

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that NRIs are prohibited from short selling securities and from trading in the currency and commodity derivatives segments. These prohibitions apply on top of the permitted NRI investment routes. The Trap: NRIs may invest in mutual funds, purchase equity shares through a PINS account, and are required to maintain separate demat accounts for repatriable and non-repatriable holdings. The prohibited items being tested here are confined to short selling and to currency derivatives trading. Note: Source basis is pp.310-312 of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook (June 2025), covering NRI PINS, demat, and trading-account permissions and prohibitions.
